producer.decline_message: terminal goal is not an Eq/Iff shape this schema's refl/symm/trans/Iff.intro combinators can close
producer.why: the goal has zero leading hypotheses (n + a ≡ a [ZMOD n] is unconditional), so after whnf-unfolding Int.ModEq to (n+a) % n = a % n there is no retained Eq-typed hypothesis for symm/trans to run over, and def_eq((n+a)%n, a%n) does not hold for free (symbolic) n, a -- unlike int-modeq-{refl,symm,trans,comm}, which only ever manipulate an ALREADY-GIVEN equality and never need to derive a new one. Mathlib's own proof is `:= by simp`, not `rfl`, independently confirming this is not a definitional identity.

existing_kernel_comparison.detail: this kernel's Int.ModEq.add_left / Int.ModEq.add_right are `∀ n a b c, 0 < n → ModEq n a b → ModEq n (c+a) (c+b)` (resp. add_right), routed through modEq_iff_dvd which itself requires `0 < n`. The Mathlib target is unconditional in n (true for n <= 0 too), which is strictly stronger than what modEq_iff_dvd supports today. F-ml430-int-modeq-one-01d9de39.json and F-ml430-int-modeq-neg-d6ff57b6.json already record this same `0 < n` restriction as the reason their siblings stay open; this fact is one of those siblings. The missing ingredient (per those notes) is a natAbs-based generalization of Int.emod_lt_of_pos (int_prelude/division.rs) that would drop the positivity hypothesis -- new kernel-level work, out of scope for this lane (crates/axeyum-lean-kernel/src/ is off-limits per brief).

disposition: epistemic_status stays open; no operation registered per ADR-0602 (admission precedes registration -- fabricating a proved status or a registry entry from a shape match alone is exactly the checker-that-cannot-fail defect this project rejects elsewhere).
next: the natAbs-based magnitude bound generalizing Int.emod_lt_of_pos (int_prelude/division.rs) would unblock this fact and its two named siblings at once, but requires kernel-level work outside crates/axeyum-lean-import/.
